parts:

possible that my PC doesn't has the memory needed to perform this
analysis??


I'll be very grateful if someone knows a solution. Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: problem with "timer"
parts:
Hi Felipe,

In the function timer() change this line:

F <- f*n1/n
to this:
F <- f*(n1/n)

R was actually to comput 44100*44100 which is too much...

You file is very noisy. Detecting the calls might no be easy at all. You
should play with the 'power' and 'msmooth' or 'ksmooth'. Note also that
timer() may be quite slow with long files...

I will fix this in the next version of seewave that should appear quite
soon.

Best

Jerome

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: problem with "timer"
parts:
No, you need to fix the function by yourself.
You have two options:
(1) you create a new file timer2.r You paste the code of the function timer()
in this file, change the name of the function to timer2 and do the
change detailed in my previous email. You source this new file with
source() and then use timer2() instead of timer() in your code.
(2) you use the function fix() that let you temporally change the code
of a function. This means you do fix(timer) and do the change.

Let me know if you could cope with one of these options,

Best
Jerome
